idiom_name: Ebean entity bean extending io.ebean.Model (Active Record style)
implementation_notes: Ebean is the JVM ORM that supports the pattern directly: extend io.ebean.Model and the bean gains instance save/update/delete plus static finders, and because Ebean is session-less with no attach/detach semantics the object is never separated from its persistence context - exactly what makes Active Record workable on the JVM. What replaces the classic structure is a base class plus an annotation-processed enhancement step (@Entity, @Id) rather than hand-written mapping; the JPA/Hibernate alternative deliberately goes the other way (entityManager.merge/persist on detached instances) and is the data-mapper norm, with ActiveJDBC as the other lightweight Active Record library.
pitfalls: Lazy loading outside a transaction throws: accessed relations need the object loaded in the scope where the database session is still open.
Bean enhancement is part of the build (the entity classes are rewritten at compile time); running them un-enhanced - some test setups, some IDE runs - fails in confusing ways.
Unlike JPA there is no detach/attach cycle, so code carried over from Hibernate that expects merge() on a detached instance silently behaves differently.
